title: 2026 legislative race ratings · Democratic swing scenarios
method: Apply user-assumed Democratic vote-share gains of 6, 7 and 8 percentage points to comparable contested 2024 D–R baselines. Each gain shifts the two-party margin by twice that amount. Keep previously rated races and add races entering the 20-point window in either scenario. The main rating uses the 7-point midpoint. Do not apply the D–R shift to independent-versus-Democratic matchups.
margin_definition: Scenario leader’s gap over the runner-up in percentage points. For two-party races this is the D–R margin; for District 15 it includes the assumed Fung share. The historical margin excludes write-ins.

notes: The 6%, 7% and 8% scenarios mean percentage-point gains in Democratic vote share, not changes of that size in the D–R margin. They are user-specified scenarios, not measured forecasts.
The Senate 17 scenarios shift the major-party baseline only; shares for the two independent candidates are unknown.
The current race has more than two candidates. This label uses the historical two-candidate baseline; third-party vote shares and vote transfers are not estimated.
